(b)Water System
The City of Harrisburg receives its water supply primarily from DeHart Dam on Clark Creek approximately six miles north of Harrisburg, and uses the Susquehanna River as an auxiliary source. A slow sand filter treatment plant is maintained on City Island, in the River near the project, where water drawn from the Susquehanna River during emergencies is treated.
The City of Harrisburg was able to maintain water supply throughout the 1972 flood even though minor damage occurred at the spillway of DeHart Dam. The filter plant on City Island was completely inundated and has been out of operation since the Fbood. The City of Harrisburg was able to supply emergency service to communities where water was urgently needed.
Like the sewers in the project area, many of the water mains were also installed around the turn of the century. Most of these are 10", 8", or 6" cast iron pipe (see Existing Public Utilities Map, appendix E). There have been some problems with water discoloration, but the mains are considered to be in fair condition and adequate for the project area as it now exists.
